page: Amazon Web Services g6.8xlarge is an accelerated computing instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. The instance is powered by a 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processor offering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning includes 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Local fast storage consists of an included 900 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. It does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Hardware acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPU equipped with 22 GB of VRAM. This accelerator configuration excels in machine learning inference tasks, placing in the top tier for small and medium model throughput. Benchmarks report prompt processing rates of 12,203.0 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model and 2,190.32 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model, with corresponding generation speeds of 470.24 tokens per second and 53.34 tokens per second. Larger models, such as 70B parameter architectures, operate with lower prompt processing speeds of 36.03 tokens per second, constrained by the single GPU footprint.

General-purpose compute and system memory metrics reflect steady midrange performance. The processor achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 2,990.03, ranking in the top 25%, while multi-core execution reached 47,873.35, aligning with median tier performance. Cryptographic hardware acceleration is evident in strong PassMark encryption testing at 37,936.6 points, facilitated by native AES and VAES instruction support. CPU vector extensions lack AVX-512 and AMX flags, which bounds general-purpose CPU matrix operations compared to specialized compute alternatives.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g6.8xlarge offers a balanced resource density for modern AI inference and graphics processing, eliminating the overhead of enterprise-scale multi-GPU clusters. Its primary hardware tradeoffs involve modest DDR4 memory throughput and a single GPU capacity, rendering it ill-suited for massive distributed deep learning training. The instance is primarily suited for deep learning inference, real-time video transcoding, graphics-intensive rendering pipelines, and ray tracing workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services g6.8xlarge is an accelerated computing instance operating on the Nitro hypervisor. The system pairs an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor providing 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores at 3.4 GHz) with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory. GPU acceleration is delivered by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 22 GB of VRAM. Local ephemeral storage is bundled via a 900 GB NVMe SSD alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier capability in small to medium LLM inference, reaching 2,190.32 tokens per second for 7B model prompt processing. Compute and memory operations perform near median enterprise thresholds, reinforced by strong single-core and cryptographic execution. The lack of AVX-512 extensions and a single GPU frame the system tradeoffs. It is well matched for machine learning inference, ray tracing, and graphics processing pipelines.
